title: Using Electrons to 3D-Print Ferromagnetic Nanostructures and Characterise their 3D Magnetic States Using Tomographic Model Based Iterative Reconstruction
content: Components in computer processing units have been consistently reducing in size and increasing processing speed for the last 60 years, but their development is approaching its limits due to resistive heating by electrical currents [1], therefore alternative technologies are necessary. Spintronic data storage devices that use magnetic domains to represent bits do not require power to store the data [2], but when a current is applied, the magnetic domains translate along nanowires at ∼100 m/s speeds [3]. This can be used to develop more energy-efficient computer components [4], therefore, we are developing methods for fabricating and characterising 3D spintronic circuit prototypes using electron microscopy. To improve the performance of magnetic nanoscale technologies, such as computer memory devices [3], it is beneficial to extend them from 2D films to 3D structures [5]. This would allow the harnessing of curvature-induced magnetic interactions [6, 7] and make more efficient use of space on chips [8]. We fabricate 3D spintronic device prototypes, characterise their chemical and magnetic structures, and evaluate their performance to develop 3D magnetic data storage technologies.
